title: Navigating Between Routes 🧭
description: Use routerLink, routerLinkActive, and the Router service for programmatic navigation.

slides.title: Linking to Routes – The Angular Way 🔗
slides.content: # routerLink Directive Instead of using `` (which causes a full page reload), Angular provides the `routerLink` directive. * It accepts a string or an array of path segments. * It prevents the default anchor click behavior and uses the router internally. Syntax: ```html Home Product ``` This keeps your SPA smooth and fast.

quizData.question: Why use `routerLink` instead of `href` for internal navigation?

options.text: It avoids a full page reload, keeping the SPA experience.

quizData.explanation: `routerLink` uses the router to navigate without triggering a browser page reload.

slides.title: Active Link Styling with routerLinkActive 🎨
slides.content: Angular provides `routerLinkActive` to automatically add a CSS class when the associated route is active. ```html Home ``` You can also apply a class to a parent element using `[routerLinkActiveOptions]="{ exact: true }"` for exact matching (useful for root paths).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use routerLink for Templates, Router for Code

Keep navigation in templates declarative with `routerLink`. Use programmatic navigation only for logic‑driven redirects (like after login).
